items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I think somewhere in there, you'll find that Ray Hindoff was really in to a lot of jazz... I think that he was instrumental somehow in getting people to Warners... I think that was where Ray Hindoff worked.

ctx.x: Anyway, he had him to do something. And then I got to the place at MGM, and I was working there so much and they -- you know, I had made a pretty good reputation, and then they wanted -- they said they wanted a good trumpet player, a good saxophone player, a good trombone player, as they would say, a "colored" guy, you know.

So I started -- I remember that Luntzwood and Basie was in town, I took -- as a matter of fact, I took Marshall Royal to the studio, you know, because Marshall Royal was an excellent musician and he could read everything they could put up there, so that's what you had to do at the studio.
